speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing right groin pain and have an abnormal leg position after a rear-end collision. Can you tell me exactly how the injury happened and what position your leg was in when you were struck?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Femoral neck fracture.

The mechanism of injury—a restrained driver in a rear-end collision with immediate severe groin pain and abnormal leg positioning—is highly suggestive of a femoral neck fracture or hip dislocation. Given the specific pain location and trauma, we must rule out hip joint disruption immediately.

REQUEST TEST: X_Pelvis (AP and Frog-leg view)
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvis_XRay
